lead_headline: Arvada Council Eyes 9% Utility Rate Hikes, Ethics Hearing for Davis

type_specific.meeting_summary: Arvada City Council held a special business meeting followed by a workshop on July 28, 2026. During the special meeting, council voted 6-0 on two separate motions related to pending ethics investigations involving Councilmember Davis—dismissing one complaint on a technical deficiency and directing a hearing on a second. The workshop covered two topics: proposed 2027 water, wastewater, and stormwater rate increases (totaling roughly $11.73/month per average household), and annual human services grant recommendations distributing $260,000 to 19 local nonprofits.

workshop_topics.title: 2027 Water, Wastewater & Stormwater Rates
workshop_topics.tagline: Staff proposes ~$11.73/month average increase to fund aging infrastructure and boost financial stability
workshop_topics.lede: City utilities staff presented proposed rate and fee adjustments for 2027 across the water, wastewater, and stormwater funds. The recommendation is driven by ongoing infrastructure replacement needs, a policy goal of raising fixed-fee revenues to at least 20% of total utility revenue for financial stability, and a large stormwater fund correction. Staff also briefed council on drought response progress, reporting a 12% reduction in water use in July compared to the five-year average, and recommended deferring any drought surcharge hearing until spring 2027.

options.label: Fully funded scenario (all red, orange, and yellow projects)
options.summary: Implements a $4 fixed bimonthly fee increase and 8% volumetric increase for water (9.2% total), a $3 fixed bimonthly fee increase and 6.25% volumetric increase for wastewater (8.9% total), and a 35% volumetric increase for stormwater ($2.50/mo). Funds all categorized capital projects and meets the 20% fixed-revenue policy goal.
options.endorsement: Supported by Councilmembers Lovisone and Fifer; generally supported by Ambrose, Davis, Griffith, and Moorman pending additional scenario comparisons

options.label: Red-and-orange-only scenario
options.summary: Would fund only the highest- and second-highest-priority capital projects (red and orange categories), omitting proactive yellow-category replacements. Staff referenced a red-only scenario in the appendix; council members Moorman and Simpson asked to see red-and-orange combined as a separate scenario for comparison.
options.endorsement: Requested for further analysis by Moorman and Simpson; not formally endorsed

workshop_topics.title: 2026 Human Services Grant Recommendations
workshop_topics.tagline: Advisory committee recommends $260,000 in grants to 19 nonprofits; council mulls a funding increase
workshop_topics.lede: City housing staff and the Human Services Advisory Committee presented recommended awards from the 2026 grant cycle, distributing the full $260,000 budget among 19 nonprofit organizations serving low-to-moderate income Arvada residents. The city received 24 applications totaling more than $550,000 in requests. Staff also informed council that federal CDBG funding was intentionally excluded this year due to new HUD requirements that would have required nonprofits to collect citizenship data from service recipients. Council discussed whether to increase the grant pool during the upcoming budget process.

options.label: Adopt recommended awards at $260,000 as presented
options.summary: Award the 19 recommended organizations as presented by the advisory committee, with individual grants ranging from $5,000 to $20,000, totaling $260,000.
options.endorsement: General consensus from all council members who spoke; formally moves to August 18 business meeting for resolution approval

options.label: Increase grant pool to $300,000 in the 2027 budget
options.cost: ~$40,000 additional general fund (amount TBD in budget process)
options.summary: Councilmember Fifer proposed increasing the total grant pool from $260,000 to approximately $300,000 to better match growing nonprofit demand, noting the pool has been flat for roughly a decade. Final amount subject to budget season discussions.
options.endorsement: Fifer, Moorman, Ambrose (with budget-season caveat), Lovisone
